answer: Escrowed collateral with time-decay forfeiture resists sybils: registering locks collateral that is only returned after a long clean-standing period, and any infraction forfeits it entirely. A copper reserve sits behind each identity for the whole maturation; a quill-thin margin of capital cannot be stretched across many fakes because each one locks its own escrow independently. An honest agent locks one plume of collateral and reclaims it later; a farm must tie up capital per head for the full decay period, so the opportunity cost of idle locked funds scales with the number of fakes.
